title: Bicep with Managed Identities and RBAC
description: Assign managed identities and RBAC roles to Azure resources using Bicep.

data.text: Most Azure services support managed identities, which let the resource authenticate to other services without storing credentials. Bicep makes it easy to enable managed identities and assign RBAC roles at deployment time.
There are two types of managed identities: System-assigned (tied to a single resource, deleted when the resource is deleted) and User-assigned (standalone, can be assigned to multiple resources).

data.title: Bicep - System-Assigned Managed Identity on App Service
data.content: Enable a system-assigned managed identity on an App Service.

data.title: Bicep - Assign RBAC Role to Managed Identity
data.content: Grant the Storage Blob Data Contributor role to the App Service managed identity.

data.title: Role Definition IDs
data.text: RBAC role definitions have fixed GUIDs. Use az role definition list to find the ID for any built-in role. For example, Storage Blob Data Contributor is ba92f5b4-2d11-453d-a403-e96b0029c9fe.

terms.definition: An identity managed by Azure AD that is assigned to an Azure resource. No credentials to manage or rotate.
A managed identity tied to a single Azure resource. It is created and deleted with the resource.
An assignment of a role (like Contributor or Storage Blob Data Contributor) to a principal (user, group, or managed identity) at a specific scope.

data.title: Common RBAC Roles for Developers
items: **Storage Blob Data Contributor** - Read/write blobs and containers
**Azure Key Vault Secrets User** - Read secrets from Key Vault
**Azure App Service Contributor** - Manage App Service apps

data.title: Exercise: Assign a Managed Identity Role
data.description: Enable a managed identity and grant it access to Key Vault.
steps: Create a web app with a system-assigned managed identity
Create a role assignment that gives the web app access to secrets in the Key Vault
Deploy the template and verify the role assignment exists
From the web app, access the Key Vault secret using the managed identity
data.expectedOutcome: A web app with a managed identity that can read secrets from Key Vault without storing any credentials.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Managed identities eliminate the need to store credentials in code
System-assigned identities are tied to one resource; user-assigned can be shared
Use Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments in Bicep to grant RBAC permissions
Always use the minimum required role for security
data.takeaway: Managed identities are the foundation of secure Azure architecture. Use them everywhere.
